trials.notes: Used the correct HTML Processor for body-fragment parsing and normalized token serialization. All WP_HTML_Processor calls are documented: create_fragment, normalize, next_token, get_token_type, get_modifiable_text, serialize_token, and get_last_error. The solution follows the documented rewrite-with-serialize_token pattern, compares decoded text only on #text tokens, and avoids comments, attributes, and special element opener text.

Same strong documented pattern as trial-1: create a fragment processor, walk tokens, test #text with get_modifiable_text, and wrap serialize_token output. No undocumented API calls and no _doing_it_wrong records. The fallback policy is explicit and stays within documented behavior.

Used the documented HTML Processor token-walking and serialize_token rewrite pattern exactly. The explanation correctly identifies that special text-bearing elements are not ordinary #text tokens in this walk. No hallucinated methods or misuse records.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 hidden cases. The docs did well in four places: the Tag Processor “Which processor should I use?” section steered subjects away from flat tag/attribute editing and toward WP_HTML_Processor for normalized output and missing/implied closers; the HTML Processor “Recipe: rewrite while serializing tokens” and serialize_token() entry gave the exact mental model for building an output string while walking tokens; get_modifiable_text() clearly said decoded text is returned for #text tokens and warned that it is not a predicate for ordinary text; and the ordinary subtree text guidance made comments, attributes, SCRIPT/STYLE/TEXTAREA/TITLE opener-carried text, and split text nodes hard to confuse with wrappable DOM text. Near-miss: all candidates added an unsupported-markup fallback using normalize($html) or raw input. That is documented as a possible explicit policy, but for rewrite functions it can discard accumulated emitted changes, so it remains an area where subjects may pass ordinary cases while carrying a latent contract mismatch for unsupported markup policies.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::serialize_token() and “Recipe: rewrite while serializing tokens”
doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn that normalize($html) after a rewrite discards accumulated changes, but the fallback choices are presented as a broad list. Subjects still added normalize/raw-input fallback branches after emitting wrapper output.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact fallback policy table for token-rewrite functions: all-or-nothing rewrite, best-effort partial rewrite, preserve-original-on-error, and sentinel/null-on-error. State explicitly that normalize($html) is only appropriate when intentionally discarding every emitted change.

doc_gaps.problem: The null-return contract is documented, but string-returning transformation examples do not show how to choose a fallback when processor creation fails.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note that a caller promising rewritten normalized HTML cannot recover wrappers if no processor is created; it must choose a documented function-level policy such as empty string, null, original input, or normalized original, with the tradeoff named.

doc_gaps.problem: Decoded-vs-raw and opener-carried special element text are explained, but the information is spread across prose and examples.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small token table in the method docblock: #text is decoded ordinary text, comments are raw token text, TITLE/TEXTAREA are decoded opener-carried text, SCRIPT/STYLE are raw opener-carried text, and tokens without modifiable text return an empty string.
